title: adaptive-grace-window-autoscaler-and-proportional-burst-metering
author: Leah Park
release_notes: Introduces a new adaptive grace-window autoscaler that reduces oscillation during transient load spikes and a proportional burst metering layer to ensure fair burst consumption across tenants. Includes telemetry for sampled utilization and commitment drift; migration adds a small DB table for grace-window state.
description: Context: Production customers with intermittent microbursts have seen oscillatory autoscaling behavior when using strict headroom policies. This PR implements a new adaptive grace-window autoscaler (AGWA) that smooths commit/release decisions across a configurable time window and a proportional burst metering layer (PBM) that rates burst consumption relative to committed capacity. Motivation: Reduce unnecessary scale-ups caused by short-lived spikes while preserving bursty tenant experience and maintaining throughput guarantees. Summary of changes: 1) controller/autoscale/agwa.go: new controller implementing adaptive grace window with a tunable growth-decay curve and soft lock semantics; 2) controller/autoscale/pbm_meter.go: proportional burst metering logic that maintains per-tenant burst credits and charges bursts proportionally to committed throughput; 3) pkg/telemetry/utilization_sampler.go: lightweight sampled-util exporter (HDR-sketch-backed) to feed SLO dashboards without high cardinality cost; 4) storage/migrations/202603_agwa_table.sql: DB migration to add agwa_state and last_probe tables; 5) config/defaults.yaml: new knobs (grace_window_ms, decay_factor, burst_share_alpha, sampling_rate); 6) e2e/autoscale_agwa_test.go and unit tests for meter and sampler; 7) operator/helm/templates/dedicated-config.yaml: new config keys surfaced for Dedicated deployments; 8) docs/observability/agwa.md and docs/dedicated/burst-metering.md. Rollout plan: canary on a single Dedicated pool (us-west-2-pool-b) with conservative defaults (grace_window_ms=5000, decay_factor=0.6, burst_share_alpha=0.2, sampling_rate=0.01), observe sampled_util_percentiles and headroom_oscillation_rate for 48h, then ramp to 10% of fleets with automatic rollback if SLA regressions exceed 2 p.p. Key highlights and rationale: - Adaptive window: Instead of a fixed hysteresis, AGWA computes an effective window length based on recent variance in per-tenant request rate and observed commit churn; this keeps the controller responsive under steady growth while adding inertia for ephemeral spikes. - Proportional burst metering: Tenants draw from a proportional share of a burst pool; credits replenish relative to their committed throughput so small tenants can't exhaust shared burst capacity unfairly. PBM also exposes a per-tenant burst_score metric to guide throttling/fallback decisions. - Commit smoothing vs immediate reservation: AGWA favors soft reservations first (short-lived local headroom) and escalates to hard reservations only when sustained demand persists beyond the adaptive window. This reduces unnecessary long-lived allocations. - Telemetry-first design: Sampled utilization (1% default) feeds a new dashboard and a degradation alert that correlates commit drift to observed latency slippage. Implementation notes: - The controller uses a token-bucket style local cache to avoid frequent DB writes; periodic reconciliation persists compacted state. - To avoid hiccups during deploy, PBM supports a passive read-only mode where it only reports metrics without enforcing charge; operator toggles enforcement flag after canary validation. - Unit tests cover edge cases (rapid alternating bursts, tenant churn, and DB reconnection loops). Estimated impact: In our canary runs on a synthetic microburst trace the AGWA+PBM combination reduced scale-up events by ~28% and reduced tail autoscale latency by ~180ms on average while keeping 95th latency within SLA. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4823) - [x] Unit and e2e tests - [x] DB migration script included and reversible - [x] Helm chart keys documented - [x] Observability dashboards and alerts added - [x] Canary rollout plan included Known limitations and follow-ups: - RBAC integration for PBM admin endpoints is pending (follow-up PR). - Sampling rate tuning may require higher sampling in noisy pools; added a toggle in config for immediate adjustment. - We introduced a very small DB table; in extreme scale there is a risk of hotspotting which will be mitigated by sharding the keyspace (next PR).
